brief.headline: Samsung/SK Hynix diverge on HBM3E momentum; DRAM/NAND pricing peak fears emerge amid 30% volatility swings
brief.summary: <cite index="20-1,20-2">SK Hynix and Samsung both clocked record single-day gains of ~30% and ~27% on July 31</cite>, then <cite index="23-1,23-2">tumbled under heavy foreign selling on Aug 6 after US chip losses showed investors had little tolerance for results falling short of heightened expectations</cite>. <cite index="11-2">Q3 2026 contract DRAM pricing is projected to rise 13-18% QoQ and NAND 10-15% QoQ, a marked slowdown from Q2's ~60% jumps</cite>, while <cite index="10-13">buyers are no longer chasing higher spot quotes and NAND spot trading has gone quiet</cite>. <cite index="29-1,29-2">Hyperscalers hit $700B+ in 2026 AI capex, with Alphabet spending $35.67B in Q1 alone and Google Cloud backlog nearly doubling QoQ to over $460B</cite>, sustaining tight HBM3E supply despite <cite index="2-9">warnings that HBM prices could enter a correction phase after 2026 as competition heats up and capacity expands</cite>.
brief.pair_trade_view: Long SK Hynix / Short Samsung. <cite index="5-10,5-11">SK Hynix maintains 62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025) and 57% revenue share (Q3)</cite>, while <cite index="4-8">Samsung's HBM market share plummeted from 41% in Q2 2024 to 17% in Q2 2025 as the company struggled to pass NVIDIA's qualification tests</cite>. <cite index="5-7,5-9">HBM3E is expected to remain the flagship product in 2026, accounting for ~two-thirds of total HBM shipments</cite>, favoring SK Hynix's proven 12H stack lead. <cite index="26-4,26-6">SK Hynix stock surged over 9% to highest since 2000 on OpenAI/Stargate partnership, while Samsung has been working to get HBM4 chips certified by Nvidia</cite>, underscoring certification risk overhang. Volatility remains extreme but the structural positioning gap persists.

memory_cycle.notes: <cite index="10-5,10-7">Conventional DRAM contract prices rose 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026, pushing total memory industry revenue up 81% QoQ to $97B</cite>. <cite index="11-2">Q3 2026 projections show DRAM contract prices rising 13-18% QoQ and NAND 10-15% QoQ, substantial gains but a marked slowdown from Q2's ~60% jumps</cite>. <cite index="8-7,8-8">Samsung, SK Hynix, and Micron have permanently redirected wafer production toward HBM for AI data centers, removing supply from the consumer market at the same time cloud providers place open-ended purchase commitments, resulting in a structural shortage</cite>. <cite index="10-13,10-14">Buyers are no longer chasing higher spot quotes and NAND spot trading has gone quiet; the defensible read is the parabolic phase is maturing, not that a peak has arrived</cite>. <cite index="8-10">Meaningful price relief is not expected until late 2027 or early 2028, when new fabs are projected to reach volume production</cite>.

brief.hbm_pulse: <cite index="6-7">As of August 2026, HBM3E costs ~$300 per 36GB stack and next-generation HBM4 is expected at ~$500 per 48GB stack</cite>. <cite index="3-3">Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix have raised HBM3E supply prices by nearly 20% for 2026 following reports NVIDIA was approved to sell H200 AI chips to China</cite>. <cite index="5-7,5-8">HBM3E is expected to remain the primary memory used in AI servers and data centers, as NVIDIA and Global Big Tech including Google and AWS expand proprietary ASIC-based AI chip development and select HBM3E as the optimal solution</cite>. <cite index="1-10,1-11">HBM4 production from Samsung, SK Hynix and Micron is expected in late 2025 to 2026, with the NVIDIA Rubin and AMD MI455X as platform milestones that will pull HBM4 into volume</cite>. <cite index="2-1">HBM3E will remain the dominant product this year even as HBM4 ramps up, with estimates suggesting it will account for about two-thirds of total HBM shipments in 2026</cite>. Tight supply persists; <cite index="6-2,6-3">HBM now represents 30-40% of total AI accelerator manufacturing cost, up from under 20% two generations ago; for the B200 with eight HBM3e stacks, memory alone costs $2,400 — exceeding the logic die cost</cite>.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix and Samsung record best days ever, then tumble 14-15% on Aug 6 amid AI earnings sensitivity
news_pulse.implication: Extreme volatility confirms memory names are now pure AI capex proxies. Foreign selling drove Aug 6 selloff after US chip losses; heightened expectations mean any HBM demand signal matters more than fundamentals.

news_pulse.headline: DRAM contract prices up 93-98% QoQ in Q1 2026, but Q3 2026 forecast shows deceleration to 13-18% QoQ
news_pulse.implication: Parabolic Q1 pricing is decelerating but not reversing; buyers balking at further increases. Spot momentum fading first, contract pricing lags. Consumer demand destruction accelerating while AI/server demand sustains floor.

news_pulse.headline: Samsung, SK Hynix raised HBM3E prices ~20% for 2026 as NVIDIA H200 China approval expands demand
news_pulse.implication: HBM3E ASPs holding firm despite HBM4 ramp expectations. China H200 approval extends HBM3E lifecycle, supports Samsung/SK pricing power through 2026. HBM4 transition delayed relative to earlier forecasts.

news_pulse.headline: Hyperscalers hit $700B+ in 2026 AI capex; Alphabet $35.67B in Q1, Google Cloud backlog ~$460B
news_pulse.implication: Hyperscaler capex up 77% YoY sustains structural HBM/DRAM demand through 2026. Cloud backlogs large and growing; AI capacity absorbed as quickly as deployed. Memory supply constraint persists despite pricing deceleration.

news_pulse.headline: TSMC CoWoS supply-demand gap narrowing from ~20% to ~10% by end-2026 as capacity expands >60%
news_pulse.implication: Advanced packaging bottleneck easing faster than expected; TSMC targeting 115K-140K wpm by end-2026, 170K wpm in 2027. Nvidia secured 60% of 2026 CoWoS capacity. HBM supply gating factor shifts from packaging to die capacity.

news_pulse.headline: SK Hynix maintains 62% HBM shipment share (Q2 2025), Samsung collapsed from 41% to 17% YoY
news_pulse.implication: SK Hynix's HBM dominance structurally entrenched through 2026; Samsung qualification struggles persist. Samsung reportedly primary HBM4 supplier for AMD MI450, but NVIDIA remains gatekeeper to volume. Pair trade setup intact.

news_pulse.headline: HBM3E costs ~$300/stack, HBM4 expected at ~$500/stack; memory now 30-40% of AI accelerator BOM
news_pulse.implication: Memory content inflation continues; B200 memory cost $2,400 exceeds logic die. HBM4 premium pricing supports Samsung/SK ASP expansion in 2H26, but volume ramp timing critical. SK Hynix HBM3E incumbency monetizes through year.

news_pulse.headline: NAND spot trading gone quiet despite continued contract price increases; buyers resisting hikes
news_pulse.implication: First genuine demand strain signal; spot momentum fade precedes contract pricing weakness. NAND now rising faster than DRAM (Q2: 70-75% vs 58-63%). Consumer affordability ceiling hit; enterprise AI demand only support.

brief.derivatives_signal: Implied volatility remains elevated post-July 31 record rally and Aug 6 selloff. Leveraged ETFs linked to Samsung/SK Hynix cut assets from ~$50B in late June to ~$17B last week per TradingView, accelerating deleveraging cited as technical pressure factor. No structured derivatives data in payload; monitor KOSPI 200 futures and ADR premiums (SK Hynix Nasdaq-listed July 10). Recommend long vol strategies given binary HBM qualification headlines and hyperscaler earnings sensitivity.
